findings.passage: In a turbulent time where voting and constitutional rights are being threatened, I will work to ensure that both are kept intact for all of the constituents in District 12.
findings.note: Campaign issues page, general statement on protecting voting rights. No mention of ID or citizenship proof.

findings.passage: So to me, as long as a postmark exists, the ballot should be counted. I don't know why you would want to limit any votes, because if you're a strong candidate, those votes would be for you, presumably, so it should just add to your count. But it literally will disenfranchise [the] voting [rights] of military personnel.
findings.note: On a call-in radio show, she says mail ballots with a postmark should be counted, and that limiting the mail-in window would hurt military voters. Related to mail voting; it does not mention ID.

findings.passage: I think that has come to light with the ballot bill he is trying to put through. He does not want mail-in ballots past election day, which totally impedes military people — especially military people who are deployed.
findings.note: Quoted in a Daily Egyptian interview, she criticizes her opponent's ballot bill over mail-ballot deadlines. The article itself separately describes the SAVE ACT, H.R. 22, as requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register; that description is the reporter's, and she does not discuss proof of citizenship herself.
